name: Immanuel
title: God with us
summary: Immanuel is a prophetic name meaning "God with us," first given as a sign by the prophet Isaiah to King Ahaz during the Syro-Ephraimite War. In Christian tradition, this prophecy is understood as a messianic prediction pointing forward to Jesus Christ, born of the virgin Mary. The name emphasizes God's presence among His people in times of crisis and salvation.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's sign to King Ahaz
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah offered King Ahaz a sign from the Lord amid the threat from Syria and Northern Israel. When Ahaz refused, God Himself gave the sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son who will be called Immanuel.

keyEvents.title: Immanuel-land
keyEvents.description: Isaiah refers to the land as "the land of Immanuel," linking Immanuel's name to God's protection and sovereignty over Judah and its territory.

keyEvents.title: The Child Born – The Prince of Peace
keyEvents.description: The messianic prophecy about a child to be born and a son to be given, with dominion on His shoulder, is traditionally linked to the promise of Immanuel and the coming kingdom of God.

keyEvents.title: A Shoot from the Root of Jesse
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesies about a future ruler from David's line who will reign with justice and wisdom, expanding on the Immanuel hope of God's presence through a messianic king.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment in Jesus' Birth
keyEvents.description: The evangelist Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14 directly and explains that Jesus' birth to the virgin Mary fulfills the Immanuel prophecy, noting that the name means "God with us".

keyEvents.title: God With Us – The Final Confirmation
keyEvents.description: Jesus himself confirms the Immanuel principle by promising his disciples that he will be with them all days until the end of the world, completing the promise of God's presence among his people.
